newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf half-year profits jump 24 percent.
newsitem.headline: Elf half-year profits jump 24 percent.

text.p: French oil giant Elf beat its own forecasts on Thursday when it reported a 24 percent jump in half-year net attributable profit, helped by good exploration activity and group-wide cost-cutting.
Net attributable profit in the six months to June 30 rose to 3.56 billion French francs ($700.8 million) from 2.86 billion a year earlier.
Last June, Elf chairman Philippe Jaffre had forecast a 20 percent half year profit rise.
But Elf's shares had been rising in recent days on expectations of an even better showing and on higher world oil prices, which were boosted by the Iraq crisis.
Its stock dipped 0.6 percent to 380.20 francs at midday on Thursday as investors took profits on the recent gains.

Elf's performance was "achieved in an environment which was favourable for the oil and gas sector but disadvantageous for chemicals," Jaffre said. "This confirms our strategy of concentrating on the development of our core businesses."
He said the group was on track to attain its goal of a double-digit return on equity by 1998.

Operating income rose 24 percent to 10.38 billion francs, powered by gains in productivity and increased oil and gas production. Higher oil prices and refining margins compensated for a poor environment in the basic chemicals sector.
The European benchmark, Brent crude, was trading above $22 a barrel on Thursday -- off its peaks earlier this week, but well above levels seen prior to U.S. missile raids on Iraq.
Jaffre cautioned that oil prices, which have been relatively firm since the start of the third quarter, could become unstable again.

Among Elf's key divisions, operating income from exploration and production soared 63 percent to 7.23 billion, helped by productivity gains and a four percent rise in oil and gas production. The impact of a 10 percent increase in oil prices expressed in francs also gave a boost.
Refining, marketing and trading swung to an operating profit of 330 million francs from a loss of 330 million francs, boosted by gains in productivity and higher refining margins.

But operating income from chemicals slumped to 1.87 billion francs from 3.28 billion, reflecting the non-recurrence of exceptional market conditions in basic chemicals at the start of 1995. Health operating income rose to 991 million from 960 million "in spite of an environment which remains difficult", Jaffre said.

In the chemical sector, he said, activity has stabilised after a strong downturn experienced at the end of last year but cautioned any deterioriation in the European economic environment would be reflected in this activity.

Finance Director Bruno Weymuller told reporters a good part of the overall profit rise was due to productivity gains and a better product mix. "These good results are accompanied by a good financial situation," Weymuller added.
Net debt stood at 27.91 billion francs, down 9.25 billion from the ($1=5.080 French Franc)
